content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents to inventory the available project documents. Identify the files containing candidate absorber specifications, calorimeter simulation results for 100 GeV electrons, and residual activation/dose information."},{"id":"s2","description":"Read candidate_specs.md. Extract the three allowed absorber materials and any tabulated material properties relevant to calorimeter design. Assign stable numeric material IDs 1, 2, and 3 in the same order as listed in candidate_specs.md, and record those IDs for later comparison."},{"id":"s3","description":"Read the document(s) containing 100 GeV electron energy-resolution simulation results. For each allowed material and each simulated plate thickness between 2 and 10 mm, extract or compute the energy resolution percentage. Record the best energy resolution and corresponding thickness for each material, plus any configurations meeting the 4.5% requirement."},{"id":"s4","description":"Read the residual dose or activation document(s). For each configuration that meets the 4.5% energy-resolution requirement, extract the residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown. Record whether the dose is <=20 uSv/h and the numeric dose rate for each viable configuration."},{"id":"s5","description":"Combine the recorded simulation and dose results. Among configurations with plate thickness 2-10 mm, energy resolution <=4.5%, and residual dose <=20 uSv/h, select the one with the lowest 100 GeV energy resolution. Record the final recommended material ID, plate thickness in mm, expected energy resolution percentage, and residual dose rate in uSv/h."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Absorber-F2","plate_mm":2,"justification":"No 100 GeV energy-resolution simulation results were available/extracted, so no configuration can be confirmed to meet the hard 4.5% resolution requirement. Among the candidates with known activation data, Absorber-F2 has the lowest residual dose rate (6 uSv/h, below the 20 uSv/h limit). I select the minimum allowed plate thickness, 2 mm, because thinner absorber plates generally improve sampling fluctuations and therefore energy resolution, making it the most conservative choice for the stated resolution goal in the absence of usable simulation data. This recommendation is conditional: it satisfies the material, thickness, and residual-dose constraints, but the energy-resolution hard requirement remains unverified.","requirements":[{"requirement":"Absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md.","status":"met","evidence":"candidate_specs.md was found and three candidate materials were identified; selected option is Absorber-F2, one of the listed candidates."},{"requirement":"Energy resolution for 100 GeV electrons must be 4.5% or better.","status":"unknown","evidence":"No simulation_results_100gev file or energy-resolution simulation document was found/extracted; no 2-10 mm configurations with 100 GeV resolution data were available, so compliance cannot be verified."},{"requirement":"Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h.","status":"met","evidence":"Recorded residual dose for Absorber-F2 is 6 uSv/h, which is below the 20 uSv/h limit."},{"requirement":"Plate thickness between 2 and 10 mm.","status":"met","evidence":"Selected plate thickness is 2 mm, which is within the allowed range."},{"requirement":"Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV.","status":"unknown","evidence":"Best-resolution values for all candidates were not extracted and are recorded as unavailable (-1); 2 mm was chosen as the minimum allowed thickness to favor sampling resolution, but no simulation result confirms it is the best."},{"requirement":"Finish by submitting one recommended material and plate thickness.","status":"met","evidence":"Submitted Absorber-F2 with 2 mm plate thickness."}]}
